region.finding: Actually inspected all 24 source and battle enlarged face and body slices across all 13 clips and six phases. Cinder Weasel has small lower white cheek and chin shifts under the muzzle and headband in hit reaction, death and victory, consistent with incorrect neck, chest and spine weights. Upper eyes, ears and snout remain coherent. Both body sets show intact arms, hands, boots, legs and large curled tail; side arm occlusion is resolved by the front view. Lower face repair required before second review.

Actually inspected all 24 source and battle enlarged face and body slices across all 13 clips and six phases. Thorn Stag has subtle lower lip, chin and side cheek deformation while its eyes, muzzle top, ears and antlers remain coherent; incorrect neck and chest weights correspond to the affected lower surface. The mane and neck bend separately and must remain mobile. All four legs, feet, torso and tail retain coherent shapes in source and battle. Death is an authored standing turn with no body collapse, not evidence of mesh tearing. Full lower face repair and second review required.

Actually inspected all 24 source and battle enlarged face and body slices across 13 clips and six phases. Stormfin Gull upper beak, open lower beak, eye rims and crown retain coherent shapes. Side blue cheek and mask edge bend and pull near the neck in attack and cast; independent side coverage detects chest and spine influence and requires candidate diagnosis that preserves flexible cloth at its neck boundary. Wings occlude the face in hit reaction and death from the side; front views retain facial visibility. Wings, lower body, feet, toes and tail remain coherent in both assets. Candidate correction and second review still required.

Actually inspected all 24 source and battle enlarged face and body slices across 13 clips and six phases. Duskwings Bat has clear eye and covered muzzle stretching during attack and cast and folding or skewing of the cheek and upper face in hit reaction and victory. Facial patches have substantial chest, spine and arm influence. Ears and headband change their relation to the eyes as the face stretches. Neck cloth must retain its independent lower fold flexion while the actual face is stabilized. Both source and battle body sheets show coherent wings, torso, arms, hands, legs, feet and tail. Full face binding correction and second review required.

Actually inspected all 24 source and battle enlarged face and body slices across 13 clips and six phases. Mossback Toad has small lower jaw and green side cheek shape shifts above the scarf, most visible in the side hit reaction, death and victory. Upper eye ridges, crown foliage and muzzle remain coherent. Lower face includes incorrect neck, chest and arm influence and requires a targeted correction while leaving the blue neck scarf mobile. Both body sets show coherent arms, fingers, torso, legs, webbed feet and back accessory. Candidate correction and second visual review required.
